'''Petr Vaníček''' (born 18 July 1935) is a [[Czech Canadian]] [[geodesist]] and theoretical [[List of geophysicists|geophysicist]] who has made important breakthroughs in theory of [[Spectral density estimation#Overview|spectrum analysis]] and [[geoid]] computation.

==Main contributions==

===Research===
{{further|List of works by Petr Vaníček}}
One of Vaníček's main contributions of general relevance is [[least-squares spectral analysis]],<ref>Pagiatakis, S. Stochastic significance of peaks in the least-squares spectrum, J of Geodesy 73, pp. 67–78 (1999).</ref> also called the Vaníček method<ref>Taylor J., Hamilton S. Some tests of the Vaníček method of spectral analysis, Astrophysics and Space Science, International Journal of Cosmic Physics, D. Reidel Publishing Co., Dordrecht, Holland (1972)</ref> and the Gauss-Vaniček method<ref>{{cite journal |author=M. Omerbashich | title = Gauss-Vanicek spectral analysis of the Sepkoski compendium: no new life cycles | date = 2006-06-26| pages = 26–30 | issue = 4 | volume = 8 | journal = Computing in Science & Engineering |arxiv=math-ph/0608014|doi=10.1109/MCSE.2006.68 | bibcode=2006CSE.....8d..26O }}</ref> — a [[frequency spectrum]] computation method published in 1969<ref>{{cite journal |author=P. Vaníček | url = https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1969Ap%26SS...4..387V.pdf | title = Approximate Spectral Analysis by Least-squares Fit | date = 1969-08-01| pages = 387–391 | issue = 4| volume = 4 | journal = Astrophysics and Space Science | doi=10.1007/BF00651344 | bibcode=1969Ap&SS...4..387V | s2cid=124921449 | oclc=5654872875 }}</ref> and 1971.<ref>{{cite journal |author=P. Vaníček | url = https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1971Ap%26SS..12...10V.pdf | title = Further development and properties of the spectral analysis by least-squares fit | date = 1971-07-01| pages = 10–33 | issue = 1| volume = 12 | journal = Astrophysics and Space Science | doi=10.1007/BF00656134 | bibcode = 1971Ap&SS..12...10V | s2cid=109404359 }}</ref> It is based on a [[least-squares]] fit of [[Sine wave|sinusoid]]s to the data samples, and mitigates the drawbacks of applying [[Fourier analysis]] for analyzing long incomplete data records such as most [[natural]] [[dataset]]s.<ref name=pres>{{cite book | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=9GhDHTLzFDEC&q=%22spectral+analysis%22+%22vanicek%22+inauthor:press&pg=PA685| author = Press| title = Numerical Recipes | edition = 3rd | year = 2007 | publisher = Cambridge University Press | isbn = 978-0-521-88068-8|display-authors=etal}}</ref> Unlike with Fourier analysis, data need not be equally spaced to use Vaníček analysis.

His discoveries in theoretical [[geophysics]], the "precise geoid solution"<ref>[http://www2.unb.ca/gge/Research/GRL/GeodesyGroup/SHGeo.html UNB Precise Geoid Determination Package], page accessed 2 January 2014</ref> in particular, enable millimetre-to-centimetre [[accuracy]] in geoid [[computation]], an-[[order-of-magnitude]] improvement from previous solutions.<ref>Vaníček, P., Kleusberg, A. The Canadian geoid-Stokesian approach, Pages 86-98, Manuscripta Geodaetica, Volume 12, Number 2 (1987)</ref><ref>[http://www2.unb.ca/gge/Personnel/Vanicek/StokesHelmert.pdf Vaníček P., Martinec Z. Compilation of a precise regional geoid], Pages 119-128, Manuscripta Geodaetica, Volume 19 (1994)</ref><ref>[http://www2.unb.ca/gge/Personnel/Vanicek/GeoidReport950327.pdf Vaníček et al. Compilation of a precise regional geoid], pp.45, Report for Geodetic Survey Division – DSS Contract: #23244-1-4405/01-SS, Ottawa (1995)</ref>

===Service===
Vaníček initiated the establishing of the [[Canadian Geophysical Union]] in 1974, and served as the [[President of the Canadian Geophysical Union|Union's president]] between 1987 and 1989.

He was the first [[Chair (official)|chairperson]] of the [[United Nations]] [[committee]] for Geodetic Aspects of the [[United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea|Law of the Sea]] (GALOS), founded in [[Edinburgh]], [[Scotland]], by the [https://web.archive.org/web/20160926061652/http://www.gfy.ku.dk/~iag/ International Association of Geodesy] (IAG) in [[1989 in science|1989]].<ref name="HarssonIAGGALOS">{{cite web |url= https://iag.dgfi.tum.de/media/archives/Travaux_99/galos.htm |title= GALOS |author= B.G. Harsson |website= International Association of Geodesy. |access-date= 3 October 2007 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170854/http://www.gfy.ku.dk/~iag/Travaux_99/galos.htm |archive-date= 3 March 2016 |url-status= dead }}</ref><ref name="HarssonIAGGALOS2">{{cite web |url= https://iag.dgfi.tum.de/media/archives/Travaux_01/Out%20of%20Section/GALOS.htm |title= Geodetic aspects of the Law of the Sea (GALOS) |author= B.G. Harsson |website= International Association of Geodesy. |access-date= 26 June 2022 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220626150748/https://iag.dgfi.tum.de/media/archives/Travaux_01/Out%20of%20Section/GALOS.htm |archive-date= 26 June 2022 |url-status= live }}</ref>

This and other activities led to creation of the technical supplement to the Law of the Sea, TALOS (''Manual on Technical Aspects of the United Nations' Convention on the Law of the Sea'') in 1982, which is on a regular re-issuing schedule by the UN. The ''Geodetic Commentary to the TALOS Manual'', largely prepared by Vaníček and published by the [[International Hydrographic Organization]] in 1996, was incorporated into the Manual.<ref>[https://www.ablos.org/services-products/ Preface to the ''Manual on Technical Aspects of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (TALOS)''], 6th Ed. (C-51). [[International Hydrographic Organization]], Principauté de Monaco, www.iho.int</ref>

The book ''Geodesy: The Concepts'',<ref name="BookGeodesyConcepts">''Geodesy: The Concepts.''  Petr Vanicek and E.J. Krakiwsky.  Amsterdam: Elsevier.  1982 (first ed.): {{ISBN|0-444-86149-1}}, {{ISBN|978-0-444-86149-8}}.  1986 (third ed.): {{ISBN|0-444-87777-0}}, {{ISBN|978-0-444-87777-2}}.  {{ASIN|0444877770}}.</ref> by Vaníček and Krakiwsky, now translated into several languages, is a standard text for both undergraduate and graduate courses in [[geodesy]] worldwide.<ref>[http://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n81-68405 WorldCat Identities for: Vaníček, Petr 1935-]</ref><ref name=citation>{{cite web | url = http://www.craymer.com/pvmedal/ | title = J. Tuzo Wilson Medal citation for Petr Vaníček}}</ref>

Vaníček also served as [[editor-in-chief]] and [[Peer Review|peer-reviewer]] for several [[scientific journal]]s as well as on numerous scientific boards and committees.<ref>{{cite book | title = Geoid and Its Geophysical Interpretations | author = Petr Vaníček, Nikolaos T. Christou | publisher = CRC Press | year = 1994 | isbn = 978-0-8493-4227-1 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=UHYRBj4D0R4C&q=%22petr+vanicek%22+%22editor+in+chief%22&pg=PP13}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
===International===
Petr Vaníček is a member of the [[International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics]], of the [[American Geophysical Union]], and of the [[Czechoslovak Society of Arts and Sciences (SVU)]]. He was awarded the Senior Distinguished Scientist Fellowship by the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], and was a Senior Visiting Scientist with the U.S. [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=genbio/>

Over the course of his career, he taught or performed research at universities and labs across six continents, including the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] and the [[USGS]].<ref name=genbio/>

In 2022 he received the Medal of the [[Learned Society of the Czech Republic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Medalists of the Learned Society of the Czech Republic {{!}} Awards {{!}} The Learned Society of the Czech Republic |url=https://www.learned.cz/en/awards/medalists-of-the-learned-society-of-the-czech-republic.html?hledat=Vanicek |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=www.learned.cz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=University of New Brunswick - Emeritus Professor, Petr Vanícek receives award for his contribution to Canadian-Czech friendship |url=https://educationnewscanada.com/social/lcy2/article/education/level/university/1/996554/Emeritus-Professor-Petr-Vanicek-receives-award-for-his-contribution-to-Canadian-Czech-friendship.htm |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=Education News Canada |language=en}}</ref>

===National===
Petr Vaníček was awarded the [[J. Tuzo Wilson Medal]] in 1996, the highest recognition by the [[Canadian Geophysical Union]], for his outstanding contributions to Canadian geophysics.<ref name="WilsonMedalCGU">{{cite web |url= https://cgu-ugc.ca/awards/jtwilson/ |title= J. Tuzo Wilson Medal |author= Past Wilson Medalists: Petr Vanicek |website= [[Canadian Geophysical Union]] |year= 1996 |url-status= dead |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20120229221939/http://www.cgu-ugc.ca/medal/intro.html |archivedate= 29 February 2012 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Since he was born into a typical [[bourgeois]] family, Petr Vaníček's wife and children requested to leave [[Communist Czechoslovakia]] during the brief but liberal times of [[Prague Spring]]. They were granted [[exit visa]] just before the [[Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia|Soviet invasion of 1968]]. The family reunited in England where he was staying on a 1967 Senior Research Fellowship at the [[University of Liverpool]]. Together, they immigrated to Canada in 1969. He has one daughter and two sons.<ref name=genbio/>

He retired as [[Professor Emeritus]] in 2002, after more than thirty years of teaching at the [[University of Toronto]] and the [[University of New Brunswick]]. He lives in [[Fredericton]], Canada.<ref name=genbio>{{cite web | url = http://www.svu2000.org/biosketches/petr-vanicek | title = Biographical Database entry for Petr Vaníček, Czechoslovak Society of Arts and Sciences (SVU) | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20110704074319/http://www.svu2000.org/biosketches/petr-vanicek/ | archivedate = 4 July 2011 }}</ref>
